title: Data Scientist / Analytics Engineer (12-month maternity leave contract)
description:
Data Scientist / Analytics Engineer

We are seeking a hands-on Data Scientist / Analytics Engineer to join our team for a 12-month maternity leave contract.

This role combines data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, and data science. The successful candidate will maintain and develop data pipelines, transform large and complex datasets, build and support business-critical KPIs and reporting, and provide analytical insights across customer lifecycle, subscription, engagement, marketing, and revenue data.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently from business requirements through data investigation, development, validation, and final reporting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot ETL/data pipelines using Python, PySpark, SQL, and AWS Glue.
  • Process large datasets from relational databases, APIs, cloud platforms, marketing systems, and application/event data.
  • Build and maintain analytics-ready datasets using Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Glue Data Catalog/Crawlers, Workflows, and Amazon Athena.
  • Write complex SQL and PySpark transformations involving joins, window functions, aggregations, deduplication, date/time logic, and large historical datasets.
  • Maintain incremental data processing workflows, checkpoints, partitioned datasets, and recurring production jobs.
  • Develop and maintain customer lifecycle analytics, including free trials, active subscriptions, cancellations, suspensions, reactivations, churn, retention, and winback analysis.
  • Analyze customer engagement and application/session activity and connect behavioral data with subscription history.
  • Develop and maintain weekly and monthly KPIs, cohort analyses, customer segmentation, and performance reporting.
  • Integrate and analyze marketing acquisition and advertising data across platforms, channels, campaigns, and geographies.
  • Develop and maintain datasets and metrics used in Power BI reporting.
  • Investigate discrepancies, data quality issues, schema changes, pipeline failures, and unexpected changes in business metrics.
  • Maintain documentation for important datasets, business rules, KPI definitions, and data transformations.
  • Continue to implement a data governance strategy.
  • Collaborate to plan data requirements for new projects to ensure no gaps in measuring outcomes.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in Data Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, or a similar hands-on data role.
  • Advanced SQL skills, including complex joins, CTEs, aggregations, and window functions.
  • Strong Python skills for data processing, automation, and ETL.
  • Hands-on experience with PySpark / Apache Spark.
  • Experience working with AWS data services, particularly AWS Glue, Amazon S3, and Amazon Athena.
  • Experience designing, maintaining, and troubleshooting production data pipelines.
  • Experience with Power BI Service, Desktop and Dax studio
  • Experience with Dax language and M Language in Power query
  • Strong understanding of data transformation, validation, data quality, and analytical dataset design.
  • Ability to work with large datasets and troubleshoot complex data issues independently.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience with Git/version control.
  • Ability to translate business questions into technical requirements and measurable KPIs.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work with both technical and business stakeholders.

Nice to Have Qualifications

  • Experience with churn, retention, cohort, customer lifecycle, LTV, or engagement analysis.
  • Experience with marketing and attribution platforms such as Google Ads, Apple Search Ads, Adjust, CJ, or similar platforms.
  • Experience integrating data through REST APIs.
  • Familiarity with additional AWS services such as Lambda, RDS/Aurora, IAM, or Lake Formation.
  • Experience with customer segmentation, RFM analysis, statistical modeling, or predictive analytics.
  • Experience with Looker and Google services.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a technically strong and detail-oriented data professional who is comfortable owning a problem end-to-end. They should be equally comfortable troubleshooting a data pipeline, writing complex SQL or PySpark transformations, investigating a KPI discrepancy, integrating a new data source, and explaining results to business stakeholders.

Because this role supports existing production data processes and business-critical reporting, strong hands-on SQL, Python/PySpark, and AWS experience is particularly important.

WORKING WITH US

At Audiobooks.com, you'll never feel tied to your desk. We employ a hybrid work policy, working 3 days a week from home (Tuesdays & Thursdays in office). We've got two stories of really bright, open space in a great location that's just a 10minute walk from Appleby GO Station, and we offer free parking. We provide our employees with healthy snacks, full benefits, and an unlimited paid vacation policy. Our close-knit group runs a fun book club and frequent lunch outings for our resident foodies. title: Programme Manager
company: Great Ormond Street Hospital Children's Charity
description:
Do you want to use your grants expertise to help shape the future of healthcare for seriously ill children and their families?

Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Grant Funding Programme Manager to help shape and deliver our healthcare funding portfolio at Great Ormond Street Hospital.

This is more than a traditional grants management role. You’ll work closely with clinical and senior hospital colleagues to understand emerging needs, develop new funding schemes and help turn ambitious ideas into investments that can make a meaningful difference to children, families and staff.

From clinical transformation and medical equipment to patient experience, technology and innovation, you’ll have the opportunity to explore new areas of funding and help shape what we fund, why we fund it and how we know it is making a difference.

**Salary**

The salary for this role is £47,674 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office.

In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate.

#### Key Responsibilities

- Lead strategic areas of our healthcare funding portfolio, developing a strong understanding of the relevant hospital landscape, and using this insight to inform future charitable funding decisions.
- Work closely with senior clinical and hospital colleagues to review significant and sometimes complex funding proposals, helping turn ideas into well-designed programmes with clear outcomes.
- Design new funding schemes and approaches, establishing the processes, governance and ways of working needed to make them successful.
- Assess funding proposals and provide thoughtful, constructive challenge around need, strategic fit, deliverability, sustainability and impact.
- Prepare clear recommendations and present proposals and portfolio updates to senior decision-making forums, including our Trustee-level Grants & Impact Committee.
- Manage funding programmes throughout their lifecycle, from application and assessment through to monitoring, evaluation and learning.
- Build trusted relationships across the hospital and Charity, creating an environment where people can explore ideas while ensuring funding decisions remain robust and evidence led.
- Stay curious about developments across healthcare and the NHS, identifying where charitable funding could unlock innovation or create greater impact for children and families.

#### Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

We’re looking for someone with strong grants experience who is particularly motivated by healthcare funding.

You’ll bring:

- Strong healthcare and/or research grants management experience, including delivering funding schemes and peer review.
- A genuine interest in healthcare funding, with the motivation to work across areas such as clinical transformation and staff support.
- Experience planning and delivering complex projects or programmes within grants management, healthcare, research, funding or a related environment.
- Strong relationship-building and influencing skills, with the confidence to work closely with senior clinical, healthcare and organisational stakeholders.
- The ability to critically assess complex proposals, ask thoughtful questions and make clear, evidence-based recommendations.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to make complex information accessible to different audiences.
- Experience supporting senior decision-making committees and producing high-quality papers and recommendations.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a varied portfolio while responding flexibly to changing priorities.
- Sound knowledge of healthcare or a related discipline and good understanding of grant management practice.
- A postgraduate qualification in a relevant healthcare or scientific discipline, or equivalent professional experience, is required.
- Experience presenting proposals and recommendations to executive, Board or Trustee-level audiences would be particularly valuable.

**DBS**- note a Basic DBS check is required for this role.

**How to Apply**

Please click on the apply button in the top right-hand corner where you will be taken to a short application form to complete.

**Closing date:** 15th October 2026

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis and we reserve the right to close the roles prior to the closing date should suitable applicants be found.

#### Benefits

- 30 days annual leave (plus bank holidays)
- A flexible approach to working arrangements.
- Access to our enhanced pension scheme
- Life assurance
- Access to various health and wellbeing schemes, including the employee assistance programme.

title: Kairīwhi
description:
Ko wai mātou | Who are we

Te Puna Reo Ōkahukura (‘Te Puna Reo’) takes its name from a place in the Kaipara Harbour, Tāporapora, that was close to the last ancient whare wānanga of Ngāti Whātua. Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei established the early learning centre, Te Puna Reo Ōkahukura in 2007.

Te Puna Reo is an accredited early learning centre that is licensed for 45 tamariki and teaches through kaupapa māori worldviews. The Puna offers 20 hours for tamariki 3 years and older and has qualified and experienced kaimahi, many of whom are of Ngāti Whātua descent.

Te Puna Reo Okahukura is a joint early childhood education initiative between Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei and the Ministry of Education. The Puna Reo is part of a long-term kaupapa (plan) of educational excellence for the hapū where knowledge and understanding of te reo māori me ngā tikanga (language and customs) are a foundation.

Te Whiwhinga Mahi | The Opportunity

We are seeking caring, reliable, and reo Māori-minded individuals to join our whānau as Kairīwhi (Reliever). This is a casual position where you’ll support our kaiako and tamariki as and when needed. Whether you're a qualified ECE teacher, currently in your third year of ECE study or unqualified, we’d love to hear from you and support your journey in kaupapa Māori education.


Ngā tino pūkenga/whēako | Qualifications & Experience

  • Passionate about tamariki and kaupapa Māori education

  • A reliable and flexible team player

  • Qualified or unqualified, all are welcome

  • Have a basic understanding of te reo Māori and a strong willingness to learn more, fluency is a definite advantage

To be successful in this role, we recognise that the following values & competencies are critical for kaimahi/employees to flourish at Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei:

  • Manaakitanga

  • Respect

  • Resilience

  • Whānau outcome focused

  • Collaboration

  • Cultural Understanding

Requirements & Checks

Applicants must have the right to work in New Zealand.

Please be aware in applying for this role, you will be required to undergo the following pre-employment checks:

  • Safety Check

title: (Senior) Data Engineer, Novonesis, Bagsværd
description:
Interested in a career that matters? Are you excited about enabling scientific innovation through data and digital solutions? Do you enjoy working hands‑on with modern technologies while collaborating closely with scientists and digital specialists to solve complex challenges? As a (Senior) Data Engineer, you will join the newly established Digital Enablement Team within Product & Process Development (PPD), an organization of more than 400 employees across six director areas and more than 10 geographical locations. The team brings together expertise in digital implementation, data engineering, AI, and data platform enablement to help shape the future of digital and data‑driven R&D across Novonesis. Working closely with scientists, local digital teams, platform owners, and data specialists, you will help create scalable and reusable data solutions that strengthen scientific workflows, improve data accessibility, and accelerate innovation across PPD.

Role & Your Impact

This is a hands‑on specialist role that combines technical delivery, technical leadership, and enablement. You will work across a diverse technology landscape that combines open‑source technologies and Unix‑based systems with enterprise platforms such as Benchling and Databricks. You will have considerable flexibility to shape pragmatic solutions using technologies such as Python, SQL, APIs and modern data‑engineering practices. In this role, you’ll make an impact by: Design, develop, and implement robust data pipelines, integrations, scalable data flows, and reusable engineering components that connect scientific applications, local solutions, and enterprise platforms such as Benchling and Databricks across PPD. Partner closely with scientists and local digital teams to understand business and scientific needs, translating them into reliable, sustainable, and high‑value data solutions. Provide technical leadership and guidance on architecture, APIs, data quality, testing, deployment, lifecycle management, and modern data engineering practices, ensuring engineering excellence and sound technical decision‑making. Strengthen PPD’s shared data foundation by identifying reusable patterns and components, while collaborating with platform owners, AI specialists, and partner teams to resolve dependencies, promote reuse, and ensure sustainable solution ownership.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

To succeed in this role, you bring both deep technical expertise and a collaborative mindset. You likely have: An MSc degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Bioinformatics, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent qualifications gained through substantial relevant professional experience. Strong experience designing, building, and maintaining production‑grade data pipelines, integrations, and operational data solutions. Advanced proficiency in Python and SQL. Experience with APIs, data modeling, version control, automated testing, and modern software engineering practices. Experience working across multiple systems and platforms while balancing data quality, reliability, maintainability, and lifecycle ownership. Experience collaborating with scientists, engineers, or other domain experts to develop technical solutions that solve real‑world problems. Professional working proficiency in English. In addition, you demonstrate: Strong technical judgment and the ability to balance short‑term needs with long‑term sustainability. Excellent collaboration and stakeholder engagement skills. An enablement mindset, helping others succeed while maintaining solution quality. Structured and analytical problem‑solving capabilities. Strong communication skills and a curiosity for understanding complex scientific domains.

Additional Skills & Interests

We Value While these qualifications are not required, they would be considered an advantage. Experience working at Novonesis or within a similarly complex R&D environment would help you quickly navigate the scientific and organizational landscape. Familiarity with scientific data, laboratory workflows, process development environments, or research systems would be beneficial, as would experience working with enterprise‑scale data platforms such as Databricks. We also value exposure to AI‑enabled solutions and broader data platform ecosystems, as well as experience developing reusable data engineering frameworks, standards, or shared services that enable scalability and consistency across an organization.

What We Offer

You will become part of a newly formed team with the unique opportunity to influence both the direction of the team and the way digital enablement is delivered across PPD. As a (Senior) Data Engineer, you will help shape data engineering practices across a global R&D organization while supporting scientific innovation and product development through impactful digital solutions. This role offers the opportunity to work in a highly collaborative environment where scientists, engineers, and digital specialists partner closely to solve complex challenges and accelerate innovation. You will have the chance to expand your expertise across data engineering, digital implementation, AI, and scientific data platforms while working with a broad network of stakeholders across PPD. We foster a culture built on curiosity, knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and continuous improvement, where new ideas are encouraged and expertise is actively developed. Most importantly, you will have the opportunity to make a lasting impact by creating scalable and reusable solutions that strengthen data capabilities and benefit teams across the organization.

Ways of Working

The Digital Enablement Team operates in an office‑first hybrid setup. Being onsite is important for building strong relationships, understanding scientific workflows, and collaborating closely with stakeholders. At the same time, we support flexibility and remote work when compatible with team responsibilities and project needs.

Application deadline: 16 October 2026.

Contact: For additional information about the position, please contact Christian Munk, PPD Digitalization Lead at crmu@novonesis.com or +45 30 77 04 33.

Our purpose guides the way

In Novonesis, we know that solutions rooted in biology can help solve humanity’s biggest challenges. Since we began more than a century ago, this has been our guide. It’s how we’ve gotten so far. And it’s how we’ll impact the future. Now, more than ever, the world needs change. And with biosolutions, the possibilities for transformation are endless.

Opportunities for everyone

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunity for all applicants. Therefore we ask you to apply without a cover letter or photo and instead include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying. We make all employment decisions based on business needs and welcome candidates with a wide range of backgrounds, including ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, or veteran status.

Explore other openings

If this position isn’t the right fit, you may still find other opportunities with us. You’re welcome to explore open roles or create a job agent to stay connected with future opportunities at novonesis.com/Career.

Choose a career that matters

Choose a career that matters - and never miss an opportunity to make a difference.

In 2024, Chr. Hansen and Novozymes joined forces to form Novonesis.

We are 10,000 people worldwide whose expertise spans more than 30 different industries. All around the world our biosolutions already create value for thousands of customers and benefit the planet. Our biosolutions enable feeding and fueling the world more sustainably, from healthy and sustainable nutrition to biofuel. Our biosolutions also reduce the use of fossil‑based resources, chemicals, energy and water. And this is just the beginning.

title: 22879 - Specialist Production Instructor Upholsterer
company: His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service
description:
Working Arrangements & Further Information

The MoJ offers Hybrid Working arrangements where business need allows. This is an informal, non-contractual form of flexible working that blends working from your base location, different MoJ sites and / or from home (please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas). Some roles will not be suitable for Hybrid Working. Similarly, Hybrid Working will not suit everyone’s circumstances. Arrangements will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate(s) and subject to regular review.

For nationally advertised roles, the successful candidate(s) will be appointed to a MoJ office location, which may include their nearest Justice Collaboration Centre or Justice Satellite Office. This will be discussed and agreed on the completion of pre-employment checks.

Some of MoJ’s terms and conditions of service are changing as part of Civil Service reform. The changes will apply to staff joining MoJ who are new to the Civil Service. Staff joining MoJ from other civil service employers will transfer onto the new MoJ terms if they are already on 'modernised' terms in their current post or onto 'unmodernised' MoJ terms if they are on 'unmodernised' terms at their current post. Details will be available if an offer is made.

Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week excluding breaks which are unpaid. HMPPS welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the HMPPS’ Flexible Working policy.

If you are a current NPS employee, this vacancy may be available on a Loan basis for up to 2 years. Applications are invited from suitable qualified staff.

The Loan/Secondment is subject to the approval of the selected candidate's Business Unit, which should be obtained before confirmation of appointment.

Benefits

Annual Leave

-The holiday year runs from 1 March. If you work a non standard work pattern your leave entitlement may be expressed in either hours or days as appropriate. Leave entitlement is calculated on a pro-rata basis and you will be advised of your actual entitlement on appointment. If you were appointed internally and your leave was previously calculated in days, this will continue to be the case.

Bank, Public and Privilege Holidays

-You are entitled to 9 days (66 hours 36 minutes) in recognition of bank, public and privilege holidays. These hours are added to your annual leave allowance. There is a requirement to work some public and bank holidays subject to your shift pattern and the operational needs of the establishment

Pension

-The Civil Service offers a choice of two pension schemes, giving you the flexibility to choose the pension that suits you best.

Work Life Balance

HM Prison & Probation Service (HMPPS) is keen to encourage alternative working arrangements. Work life balance provides greater opportunities for staff to work more flexibly wherever managers and establishments can accommodate requests to do so. HMPPS offers flexible working subject to completion of a satisfactory probationary period and NVQ

Season Ticket Advance

-After two months’ service, you’ll be eligible to apply for a season ticket advance to purchase a quarterly or longer-period season ticket for travel between home and your place of work

Childcare Vouchers

For any moves across the Civil Service may have implications on your ability to carry on claiming childcare vouchers

Training

HMPPS is committed to staff development and offers a range of training and development opportunities, including areas such as Equality and Diversity, Dealing with Challenging Behaviour, Suicide Prevention and Anti Bullying Programmes

-There are opportunities to access promotion programmes and HMPPS provides a variety of training appropriate to individual posts

-All staff receive security and diversity training and an individual induction programme into their new roles

Eligibility

-All candidates are subject to security and identity checks prior to taking up post

-All external candidates are subject to 6 months probation. Internal candidates are subject to probation if they have not already served a probationary period within HMPPS

-All staff are required to declare whether they are a member of a group or organisation which the HMPPS considers to be racist

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. Should you feel that the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you are able to raise a formal complaint in the following order

  • To Transformative Business Services (0345 241 5358 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or e mail moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@resourcing.soprasteria.co.uk);
  • To Ministry of Justice Resourcing team (resourcing-management-office@justice.gov.uk);
  • To the Civil Service Commission (details available here)

As a Disability Confident employer, MoJ are committed to providing everyone with the opportunity to demonstrate their skills, talent and abilities, by making adjustments throughout all elements of the recruitment process and in the workplace. MoJ are able to offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns.

You will be able to request reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process within the application form. If you need additional help completing the application form, please contact the TBS Recruitment Enquiries Team.

For more information on applying for a role as a candidate with a disability or long-term condition, please watch our animated videos.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.

A Great Place to Work for Veterans

The "Making the Civil Service a Great Place to work for veterans" initiative includes a guaranteed interview scheme to those who meet the minimum criteria to provide eligible former members of the Armed Forces with opportunities to secure rewarding jobs. Allowing veterans to continue to serve their country, and to bring highly skilled individuals with a broad range of experience into the Civil Service in an environment, which recognises and values your previous service in the Armed Forces.
For further details about the initiative and eligibility requirements visit:

Redeployment Interview Scheme

Civil Service departments are expected to explore redeployment opportunities before making an individual redundant. The MoJ is committed, as part of the Redeployment Interview Scheme, to providing opportunities to those who are 'at risk of redundancy'.

MoJ is able to offer an interview to eligible candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns. Candidates will not be eligible for the Redeployment Interview Scheme if they are applying on promotion.

Civil Service Nationality Rules

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals
  • nationals of the Republic of Ireland
  • nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/settled-status-eu-citizens-families
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities who have made a valid application for settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
  • individuals with limited leave to remain or indefinite leave to remain who were eligible to apply for EUSS on or before 31 December 2020
  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service

Further information on nationality requirements (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/nationality-rules

Reserve list

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made for the same or similar roles.

title: 1026 - Full Stack Developer (React & Python) · Sr · Remote · LATAM
description:
Disclaimer – Must read: Commitment & Focus

This role requires full-time dedication, with clear priority given to Darwoft projects during the established working hours. It is not compatible with other full-time professional engagements. Any additional professional activities must be disclosed in advance and must not interfere with the responsibilities or working hours of this role.

About Darwoft

Darwoft is a software factory delivering custom software solutions and IT staff augmentation services to international clients, primarily in the United States and Latin America. We partner with startups and scale-up companies to build high-impact digital products, combining technical excellence with a people-first culture built on long-term relationships and collaborative work.

Senior Fullstack Engineer (React/TypeScript/AI-Assisted Development) · LATAM

  • Location: Anywhere in LATAM
  • Work Model: 100% Remote
  • Engagement: Full-time Contractor
  • Project: FinTech · Customer Experience Operations Platform
  • English Level: Advanced
  • Seniority: Senior

Commitment & Focus

This role requires full-time dedication, with clear priority given to Darwoft projects during the established working hours. It is not compatible with other full-time professional engagements.

Any additional professional activities must be disclosed in advance and must not interfere with the responsibilities, availability, or working hours required for this role.

Get to Know Darwoft

At Darwoft, we build digital products with heart.

We're a Latin American technology company focused on creating impactful, human-centered software in partnership with companies around the world. Our remote-first culture is built on trust, continuous learning, collaboration, and strong engineering standards.

We're passionate about technology, but even more about the people behind it. If you're looking for an environment where your ideas matter, experimentation is encouraged, and your impact is tangible, welcome to Darwoft.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Fullstack Engineer with a strong frontend focus to join a high-impact international FinTech project building an internal Customer Experience Operations Platform.

The platform provides the tools customer experience agents and supervisors rely on every day to manage queues, assignments, conversations, agent availability, dashboards, metrics, and operational workflows.

You'll primarily design and ship agent-facing experiences using React and TypeScript, working within a modern, modular frontend architecture while collaborating closely with the backend services and APIs that power the platform.

A key aspect of this opportunity is the way the team approaches software development.

We're looking for engineers with an agentic development mindset: people who actively use AI coding assistants, LLM agents, automation, and AI-assisted engineering workflows to prototype faster, solve problems, generate and validate code, improve testing, accelerate debugging, and increase overall engineering productivity.

This is not simply about using AI autocomplete. We're looking for engineers who are comfortable incorporating tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, coding agents, custom scripts, or AI-assisted specifications into their day-to-day development process while maintaining strong engineering judgment and ownership.

You'll work closely with Product, CX stakeholders, designers, and backend engineers to turn operational requirements into reliable, intuitive, and scalable user experiences.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design, develop, and maintain React / TypeScript features across CX domain modules, including operations tooling, agent presence, inbox workflows, queues, assignments, and internal applications.
  • Build and evolve reusable UI components, forms, tables, filters, dashboards, and complex operational workflows.
  • Work with technologies and patterns including Tailwind CSS, Tremor, Radix/shadcn, and Storybook.
  • Apply AI-assisted and agentic software engineering practices to accelerate prototyping, implementation, testing, refactoring, documentation, and debugging.
  • Experiment with AI coding agents and automated workflows to improve engineering productivity and development quality.
  • Build data-driven interfaces using TanStack Query, React Router, react-hook-form, and Zod.
  • Integrate frontend applications with BFF and backend APIs.
  • Work within a micro-frontend architecture using Rspack and Module Federation, respecting domain boundaries and monorepo conventions.
  • Collaborate on API design and integration with FastAPI backend services, including OpenAPI contracts and BFF endpoints.
  • Ensure end-to-end correctness across workflows involving queues, agents, assignments, conversations, and operational metrics.
  • Contribute to authorization-aware UX aligned with gateway permissions and domain-level capability models.
  • Troubleshoot issues across the frontend BFF backend stack using both traditional debugging techniques and AI-assisted workflows.
  • Ensure the reliability, accessibility, and performance of agent-critical workflows running in production.
  • Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, technical decision-making, and engineering best practices around type safety, linting, testing, and maintainability.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong frontend-oriented background.
  • Strong production experience with React and TypeScript.
  • Hands-on experience actively using AI development tools and agentic workflows such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, coding agents, AI-assisted specifications, or similar tooling.
  • Ability to use AI as part of the engineering workflow while maintaining ownership over architecture, code quality, testing, and technical decisions.
  • Experience building complex product interfaces involving forms, tables, filters, dashboards, and multi-step workflows.
  • Strong understanding of modern frontend development practices and component-driven architectures.
  • Experience with modern bundlers such as Webpack, Rspack, or Vite.
  • Experience with Tailwind CSS or similar modern styling frameworks.
  • Experience consuming REST APIs and working with OpenAPI-based services.
  • Ability to debug and troubleshoot issues across frontend and backend boundaries.
  • Experience with modern state management and server-state patterns such as TanStack Query, React Context, and hooks.
  • Strong debugging, problem-solving, and technical decision-making skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with Product, Engineering, and operational stakeholders.
  • Advanced English proficiency, both spoken and written.

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing or integrating AI-agent workflows, AI-powered interfaces, or automated support operations.
  • Experience with micro-frontends or Module Federation.
  • Experience working with monorepos using pnpm, Turbo, Nx, or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with Refine, react-intl, or admin/operations-focused internal platforms.
  • Experience developing BFF layers with Node.js / Fastify.
  • Experience with Python / FastAPI, particularly the ability to understand APIs, propose schema changes, or implement small backend endpoints.
  • Experience working with PostgreSQL-backed services and transactional or domain-oriented APIs.
  • Experience in FinTech, payments, remittances, customer support platforms, or high-volume operational systems.
  • Experience with GCP, including technologies such as OIDC or Pub/Sub.
  • Experience with Docker and CI/CD in cloud-native environments.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Job Description: Senior Software Engineer


Location: Doha, Qatar (mandatory)


Position Type: Full-Time


About Avey


Avey is a deep-tech company innovating AI to transform healthcare and improve lives across the globe.


Avey is on a mission to unlock the full potential of clinical care and make every health journey delightful.


We are looking for enthusiastic, hard-working professionals who are excited to contribute to and join Avey’s mission to create a solution that will have a real and positive effect on the world.


Position Overview


We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to own product development end-to-end across Avey's API Gateway and our flagship medical products. This is a backend-leaning role for a strong Go engineer with deep fullstack fundamentals and a full command of the product development lifecycle. You'll own a product area, make architecture calls, and ship systems that will launch worldwide and serve hospitals across the GCC. This role reports directly to the CTO and the executive team.


The candidates who are either available in Qatar or is willing to relocate to Qatar should only be applying for this role.


Key Responsibilities


1. Product Ownership — 0 to 100



  • Own product areas end-to-end: from architecture and API design through delivery, operation, and iteration in production.

  • Ship across the full lifecycle, greenfield services for new products, and extensions on mature systems already serving hospitals.

  • Partner with Product, Design, DevOps, and InfoSec to turn ambiguous requirements into shipped, secure, operable features.

  • Design and build high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go.

  • Own core parts of Avey's API Gateway and the services behind our medical products.

  • Build for scale and precision, these systems will launch worldwide and carry real clinical weight.

  • Ship frontend features in Next.js / React / TypeScript when a product area needs it end-to-end.


3. Production Quality



  • Own the production quality of what you ship; testing, resilience, observability, and on-call health.


4. Technical Leadership



  • Make architecture decisions for your product area and communicate them clearly through design docs, diagrams, and design reviews.

  • Mentor engineers through code review, design review, and pairing.

  • Raise the engineering bar across testing, system design, and incident review.


Requirements



  • 4+ years of professional software engineering, with substantial ownership of production systems end-to-end.

  • Production Go experience is required. You must have shipped and operated Go services on a meaningful scale, with strong command of Go concurrency patterns and performance.

  • Hands-on experience with gRPC and Protocol Buffers for service-to-service communication.

  • Proven experience designing and operating microservices in production.

  • Full product development lifecycle experience from scoping to production to post-launch operation.

  • Strong system design fundamentals and a deep understanding of distributed systems.

  • Hands-on production experience with event streaming (Kafka or equivalent), caching (Redis), and relational databases.

  • Deep Full Stack fundamentals, comfortable shipping features in Next.js / React / TypeScript when needed.

  • Strong instincts for testing (unit, integration, contract, e2e), resilience, and observability.

  • Security-minded engineering — authz/authn, secrets management, rate limiting, and API-layer controls.

  • Working understanding DevOps practices, containerization (Docker), and CI/CD pipelines; Kubernetes experience is a plus.


Nice to Have



  • Healthcare domain experience, HL7, FHIR, HIS/EMR integrations, or clinical products.

  • Experience integrating payment gateways (regional or global).

  • Prior startup or scale-up experience.

  • Experience shipping products to regulated or high-compliance environments (GCC, HIPAA, GDPR).

  • Open-source contributions in the Go ecosystem.


Note:


Avey is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.


This job description is not exhaustive and may be subject to change based on the evolving needs of the company.

title: 23119 - Local Prevention Data Analyst: BOLD Prevention, Justice Digital, Data and Science, Ministry of Justice
company: His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service
description:
Local Prevention Data Analyst: BOLD Prevention

Location: National

Closing Date: Thursday 22nd October 2026

Interviews: Interviews likely to take place from 17th November 2026 (dates are subject to change)

Grade: G7

(MoJ candidates who are on a specialist grade, will be able to retain this grade on lateral transfer)

Salary: London: £63,343 to £70,725, National: £58,511 to £65,329

Working pattern: Full-time, Part-time, Flexible Working, Job Share

Contract Type: Permanent

Number of Vacancies: 1

*We offer a hybrid working model, allowing for a balance between remote work and time spent in your local office. Office locations can be found ON THIS MAP

Please note that unless you are an existing member of staff at Justice Digital, Data and Science, the only London location being recruited to is 10 South Colonnade, E14 4PU. We are no longer recruiting to 102 Petty France, SW1H 9AJ.

The Role

Please note this role requires you to pass Security Check clearance. Please click on the link for details.

We’re recruiting for a G7 Local Prevention data Lead, here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative, to be part of our warm and collaborative Cross-Government and Academia team, which is part of the Better Outcomes through Linked Data (BOLD) partnership.

Public services collect a large amount of data which is used to improve the quality of services offered to the public, but it is often not shared between organisations, making it difficult to understand whether certain services have been effective.

This role sits within the BOLD Prevention workstream, which supports cross-government efforts to improve outcomes for people with multiple needs. The workstream aims to enhance data sharing across organisations, deepen our understanding of individuals' needs, and provide earlier, better-quality information to support decision-making.

This role will lead the development of national-local data products with local authority partners, including linked national justice-local resident datasets, creating a single view of residents needs and experiences to surface to the frontline and developing a scalable frontline tool that can be shared with other areas. The post holder will lead analysis to the data to provide insights to support the national plan to end homelessness, reducing reoffending strategy and place based policy making.

This post requires working closely with data and digital professionals to deliver the products, as well as analysts, policymakers, operational partners, and data providers across government and other organisations.

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including:

  • A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme.
  • 25 days of annual leave, (increasing to 30 days once you have reached 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
  • Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance.
  • Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development.
  • A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms.
  • Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too!

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here. To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog.

This Post

This role will focus on bringing national and local data together and working in partnership with local areas. The postholder will lead a pilot from inception, including data acquisition, data linkage, the development of frontline tools, and hands-on analysis of multiple data sources to understand people's journeys and experiences of public services. They will also work closely with others across the data directorate and other government departments to identify use cases, assess the feasibility of future projects, explore innovative analytical solutions, and deliver analytical products.

We welcome applications from candidates to be based in either London or Leeds HQ offices (with flexible working arrangements available). Applicants must be willing to travel regularly to London and to local authorities partner sites as required.

Key Responsibilities

The core responsibilities of the role are:

  • Lead the development of linked national justice and local authority resident datasets and associated analysis, ensuring they are based on comprehensive, high-quality data, using robust methodology, and fit for operational, analytical, and strategic use.
  • Manage the delivery of data-driven tools and products that support frontline practitioners to identify need, target support effectively, and improve outcomes for people with multiple needs.
  • Build strong relationships with local authorities and other partners, working collaboratively to understand user needs and ensure that data products and tools are practical, flexible, and scalable across different local contexts.
  • Lead a small team of analysts, namely two junior analysts and any matrix managed staff, providing clear direction, coaching and support to build capability and ensure delivery of high-quality analytical outputs.

This is a new team, and you will have the opportunity to shape your role and the wider team approach and culture.

If this feels like an exciting challenge, something you are enthusiastic about, and want to join our team, please read on and apply!

Person Specification

The following experience and skills are essential:

  • A strong track record of developing and analysing large government datasets to deliver robust analysis. This includes data preparation, data linkage and manipulation, applying analytical techniques and quality assurance. You should be able to manipulate data in either R or Python (technical skills).
  • Experience of applying statistical and technical methods to deliver robust analysis to inform policy and/or operational decisions (technical skills).
  • Good demonstration of managing analytical or technical projects, ensuring clear plans and resources are in place, risks mitigated and outcomes are delivered to time and high quality (managing a quality service).
  • Good experience of managing stakeholder expectations and navigating difficult discussions, including communicating complex findings to non-technical audiences (communicating and influencing).
  • Strong leadership skills and the ability to work with and get the best out of a multidisciplinary team (leadership)

Willingness to be assessed against the requirements for SC clearance

We welcome the unique contribution diverse applicants bring and do not discriminate based on culture, ethnicity, race, nationality or national origin, age, sex, gender identity or expression, religion or belief, disability status, sexual orientation, educational or social background or any other factor.

Our values are Purpose, Humanity Openness and Together. Find out more here about how we celebrate diversity and an inclusive culture in our workplace.

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service D&I Strategy.

Salary Information**

Base salary for this role is from £63,343 to £70,725 based London location, £58,511 to £65,329 for those based on national location.

  • New entrants to the Civil Service joining the MoJ are expected to start at the minimum of the pay band.
  • Existing Civil Servants moving on a level transfer will retain their current base salary or move to the minimum of the pay band for the role, whichever is higher.
  • Existing Civil Servants who are promoted will either move to the bottom of the new grade’s pay band or receive a 10% uplift, whichever provides the greater increase.

How to Apply

In Justice Digital, Data and Science, we recruit using the Success Profiles Frameworks. We shall assess a combination of your Experience, Technical skills and Behaviours during the assessment process.

Stage 1 - Application and sift:

To apply for this position, you must submit the following as part of your application:

  • A CV detailing your career history (including any relevant qualifications). Your CV will be assessed against the essential criteria outlined within the Person Specification of this advert.
  • A Personal Statement (no more than 750 words) which should outline your experience and skills, giving clear examples of work undertaken. It should specifically address the following criteria listed below, using a separate paragraph for each.
  • Experience of analysing large government datasets to deliver robust analysis. This can include data or analytical specification, data preparation, data linking, data manipulation, analysis and quality assurance.
  • Experience of leading analytical projects, ensuring clear plans and resources are in place, risks mitigated and outcomes are delivered to time and high quality
  • Leadership skills showcasing the ability to work with colleagues from different profession to get the best out of a multidisciplinary team

A diverse sift panel will review the information in your CV and Personal Statement to assess the sift criteria specified above. We operate an anonymous shortlisting process. Please ensure your CV and Personal Statement do not include your name or any other identifying details.

Should we receive a high volume of applications, a pre-sift based on “Experience of analysing large government datasets” will be conducted before the sift.

Please access the following link for guidance on how to apply - Application Guidance

Stage 2 - Interviews:

Successful candidates who meet the required standard will then be invited to a panel interview held via Microsoft Teams. At interview stage, you will be assessed against the following Success Profile elements - Experience, Technical and the following Behaviours:

  • Managing a Quality Service
  • Leadership

Technical skills:

  • Analysing large government datasets, applying statistical and technical methods

As part of your interview, you will be asked to deliver a presentation that assesses your technical experience. Further details will be provided if successful at sift.

Appointments are made strictly in merit order. In the event that two or more candidates receive identical interview scores, the Managing a Quality Service will be applied as the primary lead criterion to determine the final merit order.

Should you be unsuccessful in the role that you have applied for but demonstrate the capability for a role at a lower level, we reserve the right to discuss this opportunity with you and offer you the position without needing a further application.

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months, from which further appointments may be made.

Use of Artificial Intelligence

Artificial Intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Terms & Conditions

Please review our Terms and Conditions which set out how we recruit and provide further information related to the role and salary arrangements.

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact digitalanddatarecruitment@justice.gov.uk

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Data Scientist based in France.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will play a key role in shaping business strategy through advanced analytics, experimentation, and data-driven insights. You will investigate the factors influencing customer acquisition, conversion, monetization, and retention, helping teams make smarter decisions and accelerate sustainable growth. Working at the intersection of Data Science, Product, and Growth, you will turn complex business questions into actionable recommendations with measurable impact. You will own analytical projects end to end, from working with raw data and building reliable data models to applying statistical methods and communicating findings. Collaborating closely with cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders, you will challenge assumptions, uncover new opportunities, and influence strategic priorities. This is an opportunity to combine technical expertise, commercial thinking, and analytical ownership within a collaborative, international, and innovation-driven environment.

Accountabilities

  • Lead business-critical investigations across the customer journey, from acquisition and activation to conversion, monetization, and retention, translating findings into actionable recommendations.

  • Analyze marketing channel performance, attribution, and incrementality across SEO, paid search, CRM, and emerging channels to evaluate investment effectiveness and identify growth opportunities.

  • Design, implement, and evaluate A/B tests in collaboration with Product and Growth teams, applying statistical analysis, causal inference, and quasi-experimental methods where traditional experimentation is not feasible.

  • Build, test, document, and maintain reliable, production-ready data models using SQL, Python, and data transformation tools, ensuring the quality and integrity of analytical foundations.

  • Go beyond descriptive reporting to explain business performance, identify underlying drivers, challenge assumptions, and recommend concrete actions that improve business outcomes.

  • Investigate unexpected changes in traffic, conversion rates, and customer behavior, developing analytical frameworks, predictive models, and data products that help teams identify and act on opportunities faster.

  • Partner with Product Managers, Growth specialists, engineers, and senior leadership to translate ambiguous business challenges into structured analytical approaches and measurable results.

  • Take ownership of analytical projects from initial problem definition and data preparation through modeling, interpretation, stakeholder communication, and implementation of recommendations.

    • Requirements:

    • Significant experience in applied Data Science or advanced analytics, ideally within a SaaS, digital product, product-led growth, or marketing-driven business, with a proven ability to influence business decisions.

    • Advanced SQL and data modeling skills, including experience designing, building, testing, documenting, and maintaining reliable data models. Familiarity with dbt or similar data transformation tools is highly valued.

    • Strong Python programming skills, with the ability to conduct statistical analyses, develop predictive models, and build practical data products.

    • Solid knowledge of statistics, experimentation, and causal inference, including experience designing and evaluating A/B tests and selecting appropriate methods for complex analytical questions.

    • Experience in Growth or Marketing Analytics, with a strong understanding of acquisition channels, conversion funnels, attribution, incrementality, and customer behavior. Experience analyzing SEO or paid search performance is a plus.

    • Strong product and commercial acumen, with the ability to connect metrics to business outcomes, prioritize high-value questions, and identify opportunities for improvement.

    • An end-to-end ownership mindset, with the ability to manage the full analytical lifecycle, from raw data and modeling to interpretation, communication, and actionable recommendations.

    • Excellent communication and storytelling skills, enabling you to explain complex analytical findings clearly and persuasively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

    • A curious, proactive, and independent approach, with a willingness to challenge assumptions, explore unfamiliar problems, and go beyond the initial request.

    • Professional proficiency in English, with the ability to collaborate effectively in an international working environment.

      • Nice to have:

      • Experience in subscription-based or product-led growth businesses, particularly in conversion optimization, pricing, retention, or customer lifetime value.

      • Hands-on experience with marketing incrementality, attribution modeling, Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), or quasi-experimental techniques.

      • Experience developing analytical frameworks or data products that are adopted and used by business teams.

      • Previous experience in a lean, high-impact Data team, independently owning both analytical projects and the underlying data models.

      • A proven track record of influencing Product, Growth, or Marketing strategy through rigorous analysis and clear, evidence-based recommendations.

        • Benefits:

        • Meaningful business impact: Contribute to a global digital product used by more than 60 million people every month, with your analyses directly informing business performance and growth.

        • Autonomy and ownership: Take responsibility for complex analytical challenges from start to finish and see your recommendations translate into real business decisions.

        • Collaborative environment: Work closely with experienced Data, Product, and Growth leaders in a team that values curiosity, knowledge sharing, and thoughtful decision-making.

        • Remote flexibility: Enjoy a remote working environment across supported European locations, with a hybrid option for team members based in Zurich.

        • Generous annual leave: Benefit from 30 vacation days each year.

        • Sabbatical leave: Access extended leave after more than two years with the company.

        • Continuous learning: Benefit from internal knowledge-sharing sessions and external coaching opportunities during working hours to strengthen technical and interpersonal skills.

        • Innovation opportunities: Participate in dedicated hack days to experiment, collaborate, and develop new ideas.

        • International exposure: Work with a diverse, global team in an established digital product environment that combines scale with the agility of a lean organization.

title: Senior Commissioning Project Manager
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Commissioning Project Manager based in United States .

In this senior role, you will lead commissioning projects that help organizations improve building performance, energy efficiency, and environmental sustainability. You will oversee projects from initial scoping and planning through execution, testing, and final delivery, ensuring quality outcomes within agreed budgets and timelines. Working with multidisciplinary engineering teams, clients, and construction professionals, you will translate technical requirements and sustainability objectives into practical solutions. You will also manage project finances, strengthen client relationships, and identify opportunities to expand the impact of your work. The role offers significant autonomy, a flexible working environment, and the opportunity to contribute to innovative real estate and decarbonization initiatives. You will join a collaborative, values-driven team committed to environmental restoration, social equity, and continuous improvement.

Accountabilities

  • Lead the full lifecycle of commissioning projects, from initial scoping and planning through implementation, testing, and closeout, while maintaining at least 75% direct project work and overseeing annual revenue portfolios of $250,000 or more.

  • Independently scope and plan small to mid-sized projects, preparing estimates, budgets, schedules, and deliverables in collaboration with internal teams, clients, and external partners.

  • Serve as the primary client contact, building trusted relationships through clear communication, transparency, reliability, and proactive issue resolution.

  • Translate client objectives into actionable project plans, balancing strategic goals with technical requirements and day-to-day execution.

  • Coordinate multidisciplinary teams, including engineers and project coordinators, while promoting accountability, collaboration, and professional development.

  • Manage complex engagements involving multiple stakeholders, locations, and distributed teams, ensuring alignment throughout project delivery.

  • Identify opportunities for additional services and integrated solutions that increase client value and strengthen long-term partnerships.

  • Draft, review, and negotiate project contracts and related documentation in coordination with design and construction teams.

  • Monitor project financial performance, including budgets, earned revenue, forecasting, and risk mitigation, to maintain financial health and achieve targets.

  • Oversee technical commissioning activities, including design reviews, integration of the Basis of Design (BOD) and Owner’s Project Requirements (OPR), equipment installation reviews, submittal reviews, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) coordination, verification of sequences of operation, system startup, functional performance testing, and staff training.

  • Uphold high standards of quality, ethics, professionalism, and client service while supporting the organization's sustainability and social impact objectives.

  • Contribute to continuous improvement by sharing feedback, mentoring colleagues, and helping strengthen team capabilities and project delivery practices.

    • Requirements:

    • Between 5 and 10 years of technical experience in building commissioning, MEP design, energy consulting, or a related field, including at least 3 years in project management.

    • Demonstrated ability to independently manage commissioning projects throughout their lifecycle, including project scoping, budgeting, scheduling, technical coordination, and client engagement.

    • Strong understanding of mechanical, electrical, and building control systems in commercial buildings, with the ability to interpret construction documents, drawings, and technical specifications.

    • Familiarity with commissioning standards and best practices, including ASHRAE, LEED, CALGreen, and Title 24.

    • A bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

    • Strong project financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, earned revenue tracking, and risk assessment.

    • Excellent communication, documentation, stakeholder management, and leadership skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and coordinate diverse teams.

    • Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities, combined with attention to technical detail and the capacity to manage multiple projects independently.

    • Ability to work autonomously while contributing to a collaborative culture centered on feedback, learning, accountability, and measurable impact.

    • A commitment to sustainability, environmental responsibility, and social equity, with an approach aligned with values-driven business practices.

    • Preferred qualifications: Certified Commissioning Authority (CxA), Professional Engineer (PE), Building Commissioning Professional (BCxP), LEED Accredited Professional (LEED AP), or other relevant credentials.

    • Additional assets: Experience commissioning large, mission-critical, or all-electric buildings; familiarity with commissioning analytics and continuous monitoring tools such as SkySpark or fault detection and diagnostics platforms; experience mentoring junior engineers or project managers; understanding of commissioning business models, client return on investment, and business case development; or experience in socially responsible organizations.

      • Benefits:

      • Flexible work arrangements: Remote, hybrid, or office-based work options, with no mandatory in-person attendance requirements. Preferred Canadian locations include Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, and Toronto, with flexibility to work elsewhere in Canada.

      • Canadian health benefits: Employer-funded group health benefits covering 50% of the plan, employer-funded Health Spending and Wellness Spending Accounts, an Employee Assistance Program, and life, accidental death, and long-term disability coverage.

      • Flexible paid time off: At least 80 hours annually for paid time off or vacation, 80 hours for floating holidays, and 80 hours for wellness or sick time.

      • Work-life balance: Flexible working schedules and two designated Quiet Fridays per month to focus on priorities at work or in personal life.

      • Professional development: 40 hours of annual learning and development time, plus an annual learning and development stipend.

      • Retirement savings: Access to a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) for Canadian team members.

      • Remote work support: A work-from-home stipend to support an ergonomic workspace.

title: Bereavement Counselor
description:
Help people find their way through grief with compassion, connection, and meaningful support.


Hospice of the Piedmont is seeking a Bereavement Counselor to walk alongside individuals, families, and our community as they navigate loss. In this meaningful role, you’ll provide counseling, facilitate grief groups and workshops, offer community education, and create supportive spaces where people feel heard, understood, and less alone.


This is primarily an in-office role based in our Culpeper office, with occasional travel to Charlottesville.


Responsibilities:

  • Provides clinical assessment, counseling and support desired by bereaved family members.
  • Facilitates bereavement groups/workshops.
  • Provides bereavement outreach to facilities by offering education on issues of death, loss, and grief and/or supportive counseling services (individual or group) to facility residents and/or staff.
  • Participates in planning/coordinating of annual memorial services.
  • Demonstrates and applies knowledge of emotional, social, and spiritual needs and responses to death and grief.
  • Demonstrates and applies knowledge of factors that indicate complicated grief and high survivor risk.
  • Maintains and updates knowledge of community resources.
  • Prepares documentation for the clinical records per HOP standards.
  • Participates in agency and community programs to enhance education on issues of death, loss, and grief.
  • Participates in IDG and staff, department and other meetings as appropriate.
  • Maintains quality and productivity standards and participates in the measurement of these standards.
  • Provides community mailings of HOP information, bereavement letters, and notices.
  • Participates in providing support to HOP staff and volunteers related to personal and professional grief and loss issues.
  • Adheres to practice of confidentiality regarding patient, families, staff, and the organization.


Essential Skills for Success:

  • Strong assessment abilities in counseling, interviewing, and communication.
  • Deep understanding of counseling approaches.
  • Knowledge of group dynamics and the grief process.
  • Intermediate proficiency in word processing software.


Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in social work, counseling, or related field.
  • A minimum of one year’s experience, preferably in working with grief and loss.
  • Clinical experience with individuals, groups, and families.
  • Available evening hours to meet client needs.
  • Driver’s license, personal automobile and current automobile liability insurance.


Typical Physical Demands/Working Conditions:

  • Work may occur in office or community settings
  • Verbal and written communication skills, including ability to use phone and computer efficiently
  • Local and regional travel and work hours that will extend into the evenings and weekends when necessary
  • Prolonged screen-focused duties in a stationary position

title: Medical Negligence Solicitor
description:
Personal Injury Solicitor – Medical Negligence


Sydney CBD | 2–4 Years PAE | Genuine Career Progression


Take the next step in your personal injury career with Law Partners


Are you a motivated Personal Injury Solicitor with 2–4 years post-admission experience and exposure to medical negligence claims?


Join Law Partners, Australia's largest specialist personal injury law firm, where you'll have the opportunity to manage your own personal injury matters, develop your medical negligence expertise and make a genuine difference in the lives of injured Australians.


With continued growth across the firm, this is an excellent opportunity for a career-focused solicitor looking to strengthen their technical skills, take ownership of their matters and build a long-term career, with potential for future leadership opportunities.


About Law Partners


At Law Partners, our mission is simple: help more Australians get the compensation they deserve.

We represent people and their families following personal injuries that can be devastating and life-changing. Our commitment to absolute client care underpins everything we do, and we're passionate about achieving the best possible outcomes for every client.


You'll join a supportive, collaborative team with highly respected leaders, access to quality work and the backing you need to focus on practising law.


The Role


Based in our Sydney CBD office, you'll manage a portfolio of medical negligence matters.

Working alongside experienced practitioners, you'll have the autonomy to run your own files while continuing to develop your technical expertise and client management skills.


Your responsibilities will include:


  • Running your own files and progressing claims strategically and efficiently.
  • Working on medical negligence matters and developing your experience in this area.
  • Providing clear, practical advice and maintaining strong client relationships.
  • Preparing legal correspondence, pleadings, submissions and other court documents.
  • Briefing and liaising with counsel, experts and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Negotiating settlements and working towards the best possible client outcomes.
  • Managing deadlines, file progression and professional fee budgets.
  • Collaborating with colleagues to deliver exceptional client care.


About You:


You're a technically capable and client-focused solicitor who enjoys running matters, building relationships and achieving meaningful results for clients.


You'll bring:


  • 2–4 years post-admission experience in personal injury law
  • Some experience with medical negligence claims, with an interest in developing further expertise.
  • Strong analytical, drafting, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • A genuine commitment to client care, empathy and achieving the best outcomes.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • A proactive, commercially aware approach to managing your practice.
  • A collaborative, down-to-earth attitude and a desire to continue learning and growing.

What's in it for you?


At Law Partners, we recognise that our people are central to our success. We offer an environment where you can develop your expertise, be supported by experienced practitioners and build a rewarding legal career.


Our benefits include:


  • Competitive remuneration commensurate with your experience.
  • Genuine career progression in a firm on track to double in size over the coming years.
  • Flexible working arrangements, including working from home two days per week after the qualifying period.
  • Strong practice support, allowing you to focus on practising law and delivering results for clients.
  • Ongoing learning and development, with opportunities to strengthen your technical and leadership capabilities.
  • Birthday leave – enjoy your birthday off on us.
  • Wellbeing days to recharge and look after yourself.
  • Paid parental leave to support you and your growing family.
  • Novated leasing options.
  • Team events and social activities, including our Christmas party, Melbourne Cup celebrations and other opportunities to connect with colleagues.
  • A supportive, people-focused culture where collaboration, recognition and professional growth matter.


Ready to take the next step?


If you're a personal injury solicitor looking to build on your existing experience, develop your medical negligence expertise and join a firm that genuinely invests in its people, we'd love to hear from you.

title: AI Fleet Platform Software Engineer

Cerebras operates AI clusters across a growing number of data centers.

As the fleet expands, the software used to monitor and manage it must scale with it. We are seeking a senior software engineer to build the platforms and tools that help our teams understand fleet health, respond to issues, and keep compute capacity available. You will own substantial engineering work across backend services, operational tools, and user-facing applications.

You will partner with Cluster Operations, infrastructure, inference, security, and data center teams to turn real operational challenges into software that works reliably at scale.

  • Build and operate software for managing large fleets of AI clusters

  • Design systems that remain reliable as the fleet grows and continue to function through component and site failures.
  • Work closely with users of the platform to understand their needs and make practical product and engineering decisions.

Skills and requirements

  • 12+ years of industry experience building and operating production software for distributed systems or large-scale infrastructure.
  • Strong Go or Python skills and experience designing services and APIs.
  • Expertise in control planes, fleet management systems, or operational platforms.
  • Experience with Linux, containers, Kubernetes, and handling failures across distributed systems.
  • Experience designing systems that handle asynchronous work, retries, and partial failures.
  • Experience with event streaming, workflow automation, or time-series telemetry.
  • Strong judgment in reliability, security, and observability.
  • Ability to lead ambiguous projects and work effectively across engineering and operations teams.

Preferred Experience

  • Building software for incident response, hardware health, or capacity management.
  • Developing dashboards and applications for infrastructure operators.
  • Working with AI clusters and their compute, networking, and hardware systems.

Location

  • SF Bay Area.
  • Toronto, Canada.

Why Join Cerebras

People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras:

  1. Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU.
  2. Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research.
  3. Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world.
  4. Enjoy job stability with startup vitality.

Cerebras Systems is committed to creating an equal and diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.
